# QUESTIONS.md — Dana Okafor, 2025 Schedule C (posted for client response)

These questions gate a small number of figures. Everything else in the draft return is final. Please answer each; for each answer I will update the return and re-run the math.

**Q1. Phone and internet business-use percentages.**
T-Mobile ($1,020.00/yr) and Spectrum internet ($840.00/yr) are used for both the business and personally. What percentage of 2025 use was for business? (Dana's email describes mixed use; I cannot take a deduction percentage you haven't stated. Pub 463's 2% de minimis rule covers cell phones under 24a, but the business-use split must come from you.)

**Q2. Mileage log, page 2.**
Your notebook photo shows 4,860 total miles, but the "misc errands (see pg 2)" line says the detail is on page 2, which isn't in the photo. Please photograph page 2 and send it. Those 1,150 miles are currently $0 because I can't tell what they are. (Note: IRS Notice 2025-5 sets the 2025 business auto rate at **$0.70**, not the $0.655 shown on your log — I've already fixed that.)

**Q3. Is your home office your principal place of business?**
You work mostly from home and pay $2,800/yr for coworking space. If your home office (used regularly and exclusively for the business — do you have one?) is your principal place of business, then trips from home to the coworking space and to client sites are business mileage — that adds up to **2,232 miles** on top of the 278 client-site miles I already claimed. If you have a qualifying home office, there may also be a home-office deduction (Part V / line 30) — that computation rule is not in my research library, so I would need to verify it before claiming it. Do you have a dedicated home office, and did you ever work from the coworking space before or between your Larkspur shifts (the Larkspur commute is never deductible)?

**Q4. Travel substantiation.**
(a) June 30 United AUS→DEN, $389 — what was the business purpose? I see no Austin business payments or Austin client trips in the records; without a documented business purpose I've left this at $0.
(b) October San Francisco (DesignWeek): you said the conference was for client work, so I claimed airfare $412 + hotel $618 as travel assuming the trip's **primary purpose was business** (the Oct 17–18 weekend around the Oct 19–21 conference is not, by itself, a personal-activity day under the instructions). Confirm the primary purpose was business, and confirm whether the Oct 22 return flight was $377 (a United charge that date) — it isn't in the export.
(c) Marina Deli $64 on Oct 21 — was this a business meal with a business associate present (who, and what business)? 50% limit applies; currently $32.

**Q5. "Client dinner — Beacon," Oct 20, $0.00.**
The export shows this entry with a $0.00 amount and no matching card charge. What was the actual amount, and how was it paid? (A business meal with Beacon present would be deductible at 50%.)

**Q6. MacBook Pro (Aug 22, $2,149.00).**
I've expensed it on line 27a under the de minimis safe harbor (≤$2,500) rather than depreciating it. Was it used 100% for business? (If business use is under 100%, or if you'd rather depreciate, tell me — depreciation rules aren't in my research library, so safe harbor is what I can support here.)

**Q7. Health insurance after April.**
BCBS premiums ran through 2025 at $3,040/yr. You left Larkspur in April. Self-employed health insurance eligibility depends on rules not included in my research library, so the draft puts all $3,040 on Schedule 1 and none on Schedule C line 15. Were you eligible (or able to elect continuation) for any employer-sponsored plan through Larkspur or a spouse's plan at any time in 2025?

**Q8. Tartine, Sep 25, $126.00.**
Labeled just "coffee." Was this a business meal (who was present, what business)? If it's personal, it stays off Schedule C — currently it is off the return.

**Q9. Confirm Beacon and Orchard were paid through PayHub.**
Beacon's 1099-NEC ($18,500) and Orchard's ($12,200) payments match PayHub gross receipts exactly, and no separate Beacon/Orchard deposits hit your bank. Please confirm those two clients paid you via PayHub links/invoices, so I'm right to count that $30,700 only once (it's inside the 1099-K, not additional income).

**Q10. Other payment methods.**
The export only covers the First Meridian checking account. Do you pay for business items (gas — you claimed mileage, so no gas deduction either way; print shop; supplies) with a personal card or cash? If yes, send those records; a print-shop or supply deduction of a few hundred dollars is likely missing.

**Q11. Missing December 2025 activity.**
The export stops at Dec 12 even though it's labeled through January. Please send transactions for Dec 12–31: any PayHub payout, client payment, or business purchase in that window changes gross receipts and expenses. (Also: the Oct 22 United return flight, if it was $377 — I don't see it in the export.)
answer:
Oh — yes, the ~1,200 miles Jan–April were me driving to the Larkspur office every day. I guess that's commuting? The rest is client stuff and the coworking space.
Phone and internet are maybe 60% work? I don't have a separate line.
Denver was my cousin's wedding, nothing work-related.
Beacon and Orchard both pay me through PayHub. Tessaro pays by bank transfer.
That's my own health plan after I left Larkspur. Not through any employer.
For questions not answered above, the client has no additional information. Flag remaining unknowns explicitly.
